Thoroughly review the OnscreenTranslator.Linux Avalonia UI code. Focus on:
1. Program.cs — startup flow, platform services wiring, correctness
2. App.axaml / App.cs — Avalonia application lifecycle, design-time support
3. MainWindow.axaml / MainWindow.axaml.cs — UI binding, event handlers, async capture flow, remote config panel visibility logic
4. LinuxPlatformServices.cs — screenshot commands (maim/grim/import fallback), IsWayland() detection, XorCrypt, RunCommand robustness
5. GtkOverlayHandle.cs — the stub implementation, what's missing for real overlay rendering
6. LinuxHotkeyRegistration.cs — polling approach, whether it's viable
7. LinuxTrayIcon.cs — stub completeness

Flag bugs, architectural problems, X11/Wayland compatibility gaps, and suggest concrete fixes. Be critical.

childReport.diffSummary: No changes made — review-only inspection of OnscreenTranslator.Linux Avalonia UI codebase
reviewFindings: blocker: LinuxPlatformServices.cs + MainWindow.axaml.cs — System.Drawing.Common throws PlatformNotSupportedException on .NET 8 Linux without EnableUnixSupport runtime switch; runtimeconfig.json missing the switch
bug: LinuxPlatformServices.cs:26 and MainWindow.axaml.cs:50 — Path.GetTempFileName()+".png" leaks original temp file, never deleted
bug: LinuxPlatformServices.cs:44-47 — Dead code: first `args` variable computed but never used, `toolArgs` used instead
bug: LinuxPlatformServices.cs:32 — Wayland path never checks if grim is installed, will throw if missing
bug: MainWindow.axaml.cs:55 — No delay between Hide() and capture; window may appear in screenshot
note: GtkOverlayHandle.cs — Complete stub, overlay feature non-functional
note: LinuxHotkeyRegistration.cs — PollLoop is no-op, hotkeys non-functional
note: LinuxTrayIcon.cs — Complete stub, tray icon non-functional
note: LinuxPlatformServices.cs:120-134 — RunCommandAndRead potential deadlock: stderr redirected but never read before WaitForExit
note: MainWindow.axaml.cs — Remote server fields only persist on Settings click, not on combo change
childReport.manualNotes: The Linux port is structurally sound (correct Avalonia patterns, clean startup, proper interface wiring) but has one critical runtime blocker (System.Drawing.Common) and three major feature gaps (overlay, hotkeys, tray). The three stubs (GtkOverlayHandle, LinuxHotkeyRegistration, LinuxTrayIcon) represent the majority of remaining work for a usable Linux build.
